The patient reports experiencing panic attacks about three times a week for the last six months, characterized by racing heart, sweating, and a sensation of impending doom. The patient avoids driving on the highway due to these symptoms. The patient consumes three to four glasses of wine on weekends and approximately four cups of coffee daily.

The patient denies any thoughts of suicide. The patient mentions a history of a sister attempting suicide with pills during high school, which was traumatic for the family. The patient has not taken medication for anxiety since a primary care doctor prescribed Xanax for two weeks last year, which the patient discontinued due to grogginess. The patient has not had any hospitalizations or therapy sessions in the past two years.

The provider suggests escitalopram ten milligrams daily for the patient's panic disorder, noting the patient's preference over cognitive behavioral therapy alone. The patient agrees to start the medication. The provider proposes a follow-up appointment in three weeks.

paragraphs.label: Risks / benefits / alternatives discussed
paragraphs.text: Nausea and sexual side effects were discussed. Cognitive behavioral therapy alone was mentioned as an alternative.

paragraphs.label: Patient preference / consent / refusal
paragraphs.text: The patient prefers to start the medicine and consents to the treatment.

paragraphs.text: The patient denies any current suicidal thoughts.
